column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|03-02|1855|Νικόλαος Α΄|Nicholas I|Nicholas I was tsar of Russia from 1825 to 1855. He was authoritarian and conservative and suppressed the Decembrist revolt. In foreign policy he led Russia in the Crimean War, which was still under way when he died.

bio|03-02|1930|Ντ. Χ. Λώρενς|D. H. Lawrence|D. H. Lawrence was an English writer. He wrote the novels "Sons and Lovers", "Lady Chatterley's Lover" and "Women in Love", which caused scandal because of their subject matter. He died in France in 1930.

bio|03-02|1931|Μιχαήλ Γκορμπατσόφ|Mikhail Gorbachev|Mikhail Gorbachev was the last leader of the Soviet Union, from 1985 to 1991. He implemented the policies of "perestroika" and "glasnost" and brought the Cold War to an end. In 1990 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|03-02|1937|Αμπντελαζίζ Μπουτεφλίκα|Abdelaziz Bouteflika|Abdelaziz Bouteflika was an Algerian politician. He was president of Algeria from 1999 to 2019, when he resigned after mass demonstrations, following serious health problems.

bio|03-02|1968|Ντάνιελ Κρεγκ|Daniel Craig|Daniel Craig is an English actor. He played James Bond in five films, from "Casino Royale" in 2006 to "No Time to Die" in 2021. He also appeared in the film "Knives Out".

bio|03-02|1982|Φίλιπ Κ. Ντικ|Philip K. Dick|Philip K. Dick was an American science fiction writer. His works examine the nature of reality and identity. Films such as "Blade Runner" and "Total Recall" were based on his books.

bio|03-03|1703|Ρόμπερτ Χουκ|Robert Hooke|Robert Hooke was an English physicist and inventor. In his book "Micrographia" he described the cell, and he formulated Hooke's law of elasticity. He had sharp disagreements with Newton.

bio|03-03|1706|Γιόχαν Πάχελμπελ|Johann Pachelbel|Johann Pachelbel was a German organist and composer of the Baroque period. He is known for the "Canon in D", one of the most popular pieces of classical music. He was the teacher of Johann Christoph Bach.

bio|03-03|1845|Γκέοργκ Κάντορ|Georg Cantor|Georg Cantor was a German mathematician born in Saint Petersburg. He founded set theory and proved that there are different sizes of infinity. His ideas were revolutionary.

bio|03-03|1847|Αλεξάντερ Γκράχαμ Μπελ|Alexander Graham Bell|Alexander Graham Bell was born in Scotland and emigrated to Canada and the United States. He was a teacher of the deaf and an inventor, and in 1876 he received a patent for the telephone. He founded the Bell company.

bio|03-03|1953|Ζίκο|Zico|Zico, whose real name is Arthur Antunes Coimbra, is a former Brazilian footballer. He played as a midfielder for Flamengo and the Brazilian national team and was one of the best of his era. He later became a coach.

bio|03-03|1982|Τζέσικα Μπίελ|Jessica Biel|Jessica Biel is an American actress. She became known for the series "7th Heaven" and appeared in films such as "Terminator Salvation" and "The Miracle of Lion".

bio|03-03|1983|Hergé|Herge|Herge, whose real name was Georges Remi, was a Belgian cartoonist. He created "Tintin", a comic series about a young journalist and his dog Snowy, which became one of the most popular comics in Europe.

bio|03-03|1996|Μαργκερίτ Ντυράς|Marguerite Duras|Marguerite Duras was a French writer and director. She wrote the novel "The Lover", which won the Goncourt Prize in 1984, and the screenplay for the film "Hiroshima mon amour".

bio|03-03|1997|Καμίλα Καμπέγιο|Camila Cabello|Camila Cabello was born in Cuba and grew up in Mexico and the United States. She started in the group Fifth Harmony and became a soloist with hits such as "Havana" and "Senorita".

bio|03-04|1193|Σαλαντίν|Saladin|Saladin was sultan of Egypt and Syria and founded the Ayyubid dynasty. In 1187 he defeated the Crusaders at the Battle of Hattin and captured Jerusalem. He was known for his chivalrous behaviour.

bio|03-04|1678|Αντόνιο Βιβάλντι|Antonio Vivaldi|Antonio Vivaldi was born in Venice and was a Baroque composer and violinist. He was a priest and taught at a girls' orphanage. He wrote hundreds of concertos, such as "The Four Seasons".

bio|03-04|1769|Μεχμέτ Αλή Πασάς|Muhammad Ali Pasha|Muhammad Ali was born in Kavala and became pasha of Egypt in 1805. He founded the dynasty that ruled Egypt until 1952 and modernised the country. In 1825 he sent his son Ibrahim to Greece to suppress the Revolution.

bio|03-04|1832|Ζαν-Φρανσουά Σαμπολιόν|Jean-Francois Champollion|Jean-Francois Champollion was a French scholar. In 1822 he deciphered the hieroglyphs of Egypt, with the help of the Rosetta Stone. He is regarded as the founder of Egyptology.

bio|03-04|1852|Νικολάι Γκόγκολ|Nikolai Gogol|Nikolai Gogol was a Russian writer of Ukrainian origin. He wrote the novel "Dead Souls", the play "The Government Inspector" and the short story "The Overcoat". His works influenced Russian literature.

bio|03-04|1938|Αλφά Κοντέ|Alpha Conde|Alpha Conde is a politician from Guinea. He was the leader of the opposition and in 2010 became the first democratically elected president of Guinea. He governed until 2021, when he was overthrown in a coup.

bio|03-04|1948|Αντονέν Αρτώ|Antonin Artaud|Antonin Artaud was a French poet, actor and theorist of the theatre. He created the "theatre of cruelty" and wrote "The Theatre and Its Double". He had a significant influence on experimental theatre.

bio|03-04|1954|Φρανσουά Φιγιόν|Francois Fillon|Francois Fillon is a French centre-right politician. He was prime minister of France under President Nicolas Sarkozy from 2007 to 2012 and a candidate for the presidency in 2017.

bio|03-05|1133|Ερρίκος Β΄|Henry II|Henry II was king of England from 1154 to 1189 and the first of the Plantagenet dynasty. He strengthened royal justice and came into conflict with Archbishop Thomas Becket.

bio|03-05|1512|Γεράρδος Μερκάτορ|Gerardus Mercator|Gerardus Mercator was a Flemish cartographer. In 1569 he presented the "Mercator projection", a world map that was used especially for navigation. He also introduced the term "atlas" for a collection of maps.

bio|03-05|1685|Γκέοργκ Φρήντριχ Χαίντελ|George Frideric Handel|George Frideric Handel was born in Germany and lived in England. He was a Baroque composer and wrote operas and oratorios, such as "Messiah". "Water Music" and "Music for the Royal Fireworks" are especially well known.

bio|03-05|1827|Πιέρ Σιμόν Λαπλάς|Pierre-Simon Laplace|Pierre-Simon Laplace was a French mathematician and astronomer. He wrote "Celestial Mechanics" and developed probability theory. He was known for his view of nature as "determinism".

bio|03-05|1871|Ρόζα Λούξεμπουργκ|Rosa Luxemburg|Rosa Luxemburg was born in Poland and became a Marxist thinker and activist in Germany. She founded the Spartacus League and was murdered in 1919 during the Berlin uprising.

bio|03-05|1922|Πιερ Πάολο Παζολίνι|Pier Paolo Pasolini|Pier Paolo Pasolini was an Italian writer, poet and film director. He directed "The Gospel According to Matthew" and "Salo". He was controversial for his political views and was murdered in 1975.

bio|03-05|1953|Ιωσήφ Στάλιν|Joseph Stalin|Joseph Stalin was the leader of the Soviet Union from the 1920s until his death. He ruled in an authoritarian way, with extensive purges and labour camps. He led the USSR in the Second World War.

bio|03-05|1966|Άννα Αχμάτοβα|Anna Akhmatova|Anna Akhmatova was a Russian poet, one of the most important of the twentieth century. Her poem "Requiem" describes the suffering of the Stalin era. Despite persecution, she continued to write.

bio|03-05|2013|Ούγκο Τσάβες|Hugo Chavez|Hugo Chavez was a Venezuelan soldier and politician. He was president of Venezuela from 1999 until his death and led the "Bolivarian Revolution" with a socialist programme. He died of cancer in 2013.

bio|03-06|1040|Αλχαζέν|Alhazen|Alhazen, that is Ibn al-Haytham, was an Arab physicist and astronomer. In his "Book of Optics" he explained how vision works and established the experimental method in optics. He influenced the study of light in the West.

bio|03-06|1475|Μιχαήλ Άγγελος|Michelangelo|Michelangelo was born near Arezzo in Tuscany. He was a sculptor, painter and architect of the Renaissance. He created "David", the frescoes of the Sistine Chapel and the dome of Saint Peter's.

bio|03-06|1806|Ελίζαμπεθ Μπάρετ Μπράουνινγκ|Elizabeth Barrett Browning|Elizabeth Barrett Browning was an English poet of the Victorian era. She wrote "Sonnets from the Portuguese", love poems addressed to her husband Robert Browning, and the lengthy poetic collection "Aurora Leigh".

bio|03-06|1888|Λουίζα Μέι Άλκοτ|Louisa May Alcott|Louisa May Alcott was an American writer. She wrote the novel "Little Women", which was based on her family. She was also an activist against slavery and for women's rights.

bio|03-06|1927|Γκαμπριέλ Γκαρσία Μάρκες|Gabriel Garcia Marquez|Gabriel Garcia Marquez was a Colombian writer. He wrote the novel "One Hundred Years of Solitude" and "Love in the Time of Cholera", with magical realism. In 1982 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-06|1937|Βαλεντίνα Τερεσκόβα|Valentina Tereshkova|Valentina Tereshkova is a Russian cosmonaut. In 1963 she became the first woman to fly into space, aboard the spacecraft Vostok 6. She later became involved in politics.

bio|03-06|1972|Σακίλ Ο'Νιλ|Shaquille O'Neal|Shaquille O'Neal is a former American basketball player. He was tall and powerful and played for the Los Angeles Lakers and the Miami Heat. He won four NBA championships.

bio|03-06|1973|Περλ Μπακ|Pearl Buck|Pearl Buck was an American writer who grew up in China. She wrote the novel "The Good Earth", for which she won the Pulitzer Prize, and in 1938 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-06|1982|Άυν Ραντ|Ayn Rand|Ayn Rand died in New York in 1982. She was born in Russia and lived in the United States. She wrote the novels "The Fountainhead" and "Atlas Shrugged" and founded the philosophy of "Objectivism".

bio|03-07|161|Αντωνίνος ο Ευσεβής|Antoninus Pius|Antoninus Pius was a Roman emperor from 138 to 161. His reign was peaceful and stable, and in Britain he built the Antonine Wall. He was succeeded by Marcus Aurelius.

bio|03-07|1274|Θωμάς Ακινάτης|Thomas Aquinas|Thomas Aquinas was an Italian Dominican friar and theologian. In his "Summa Theologiae" he combined Christian theology with the philosophy of Aristotle. The Catholic Church honours him as a saint.

bio|03-07|1785|Αλεσσάντρο Μαντσόνι|Alessandro Manzoni|Alessandro Manzoni was an Italian writer. He wrote the historical novel "The Betrothed", one of the most important works of Italian literature. He also influenced the unification of the Italian language.
bio|03-07|1850|Τόμας Μάζαρικ|Tomas Masaryk|Tomas Masaryk was a Czech philosopher and politician. He was the founder and first president of Czechoslovakia, from 1918 to 1935.

bio|03-07|1872|Πητ Μοντριάν|Piet Mondrian|Piet Mondrian was a Dutch painter. He was a founder of the De Stijl group and developed an abstract art with straight lines and primary colours. His works include the "Compositions" with red, blue and yellow rectangles.

bio|03-07|1875|Μορίς Ραβέλ|Maurice Ravel|Maurice Ravel was a French composer. He wrote "Bolero", "Pavane for a Dead Princess" and the orchestration of "Pictures at an Exhibition". He was a specialist in orchestration.

bio|03-07|1952|Παραμχάνσα Γιογκανάντα|Paramahansa Yogananda|Paramahansa Yogananda was an Indian yoga teacher. He moved to the United States in 1920 and wrote the book "Autobiography of a Yogi". He founded the Self-Realization Fellowship.

bio|03-07|1970|Ρέιτσελ Βάις|Rachel Weisz|Rachel Weisz is an English actress. She became known for the film "The Mummy" and won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for "The Constant Gardener". She also appeared in "Black Widow".

bio|03-07|1999|Στάνλεϊ Κούμπρικ|Stanley Kubrick|Stanley Kubrick was an American director who lived in England. He directed "2001: A Space Odyssey", "A Clockwork Orange" and "The Shining". He died in 1999.

bio|03-08|1575|Γιάκομπ Μπέμε|Jakob Bohme|Jakob Bohme was a German mystic and theologian. He was by trade a shoemaker and wrote books with mystical content, such as "Aurora". He influenced Romanticism and philosophy.

bio|03-08|1869|Εκτόρ Μπερλιόζ|Hector Berlioz|Hector Berlioz was a French composer of the Romantic period. He wrote the "Symphonie fantastique" and "The Damnation of Faust". He was an innovator in orchestration and wrote a treatise on the subject.

bio|03-08|1874|Μίλαρντ Φίλμορ|Millard Fillmore|Millard Fillmore, the 13th president of the United States, died in Buffalo in 1874. He had become president in 1850, after the death of Zachary Taylor, and signed laws that formed the Compromise of 1850.

bio|03-08|1879|Ότο Χαν|Otto Hahn|Otto Hahn was a German chemist. In 1938, together with Fritz Strassmann, he discovered the splitting of uranium, which led to nuclear energy. In 1944 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

bio|03-08|1929|Ήβη Καμάργο|Ebe Camargo|Ebe Camargo was a Brazilian actress, singer and television presenter. She became known on Brazilian television and cinema and was one of the country's biggest stars.

bio|03-08|1930|Ουίλιαμ Χάουαρντ Ταφτ|William Howard Taft|William Howard Taft was the 27th president of the United States, from 1909 to 1913. He later became the only former president to serve as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court. He died in 1930.

bio|03-08|1990|Πέτρα Κβίτοβα|Petra Kvitova|Petra Kvitova is a Czech tennis champion. She won Wimbledon twice, in 2011 and 2014, and reached first place in the world rankings. In 2016 she was injured in a knife attack.

bio|03-09|1454|Αμέριγκο Βεσπούτσι|Amerigo Vespucci|Amerigo Vespucci was born in Florence. He was an explorer and cartographer who made voyages to South America. He argued that the region was a new continent, and America took its name from his.

bio|03-09|1814|Ταράς Σεβτσένκο|Taras Shevchenko|Taras Shevchenko was a Ukrainian poet and painter. He was born a serf and became the national poet of Ukraine, with the collection "Kobzar". He was exiled by the tsar because of his poems.

bio|03-09|1851|Χανς Κρίστιαν Έρστεντ|Hans Christian Orsted|Hans Christian Orsted was a Danish physicist. In 1820 he discovered that an electric current creates a magnetic field, linking electricity with magnetism. The unit of magnetic field strength is named after him.

bio|03-09|1888|Γουλιέλμος Α΄|William I|William I was king of Prussia from 1861 and, after the victory over France in 1871, the first emperor of a united Germany. His chancellor Otto von Bismarck played an important role in government.

bio|03-09|1890|Βιτσισλάφ Μόλοτοφ|Vyacheslav Molotov|Vyacheslav Molotov was a Soviet politician. He was foreign minister under Stalin and signed the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact with Nazi Germany in 1939. The "Molotov cocktail" is named after him.

bio|03-09|1934|Γιούρι Γκαγκάριν|Yuri Gagarin|Yuri Gagarin was a Soviet cosmonaut. On 12 April 1961 he became the first human to travel into space, aboard Vostok 1. He was killed in a training flight in 1968.

bio|03-09|1943|Μπόμπι Φίσερ|Bobby Fischer|Bobby Fischer was an American chess player and world champion from 1972 to 1975. He defeated Boris Spassky in Reykjavik, in a match that attracted worldwide interest.

bio|03-09|1992|Μεναχέμ Μπέγκιν|Menachem Begin|Menachem Begin was an Israeli politician. He was prime minister from 1977 to 1983 and in 1978 signed the Camp David Accords with Egypt. In 1978 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize together with Anwar Sadat.

bio|03-09|1994|Τσαρλς Μπουκόφσκι|Charles Bukowski|Charles Bukowski was an American poet and writer of German origin. He wrote poetry and novels, such as "Post Office", which describe the life of the marginalised people of Los Angeles.

bio|03-10|1845|Αλέξανδρος Γ΄|Alexander III|Alexander III was tsar of Russia from 1881 to 1894, after the murder of his father Alexander II. He was conservative and strengthened nationalism. His reign was peaceful compared with the others.

bio|03-10|1861|Ταράς Σεβτσένκο|Taras Shevchenko|Taras Shevchenko died in Saint Petersburg in 1861, one day before the forty-seventh anniversary of his birth. He is the national poet of Ukraine and is of great importance for the Ukrainian language and identity.

bio|03-10|1940|Τσακ Νόρις|Chuck Norris|Chuck Norris is an American actor and martial arts champion. He became known for action films and for the television series "Walker, Texas Ranger". On the internet there is a whole genre of jokes about him.

bio|03-10|1940|Μιχαήλ Μπουλγκάκοφ|Mikhail Bulgakov|Mikhail Bulgakov was a Russian writer. He wrote the novel "The Master and Margarita", a satire of Soviet society, which was published after his death. He died in 1940.

bio|03-10|1957|Οσάμα μπιν Λάντεν|Osama bin Laden|Osama bin Laden was born in Saudi Arabia. He founded al-Qaeda and is considered the mastermind of the attacks of 11 September 2001. He was killed in 2011 by American special forces in Pakistan.

bio|03-10|1958|Σάρον Στόουν|Sharon Stone|Sharon Stone is an American actress. She became famous with the film "Basic Instinct" in 1992 and was nominated for an Oscar for "Casino". She also appeared in "Total Recall".

bio|03-10|1966|Φριτς Φρέντερικ Ζερνίκε|Frits Zernike|Frits Zernike was a Dutch physicist. He invented the phase-contrast microscope, which makes it possible to observe transparent cells. In 1953 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|03-10|1981|Σαμουέλ Ετό|Samuel Eto'o|Samuel Eto'o is a former Cameroonian footballer. He played for Barcelona and Inter and won the Champions League three times. He is the all-time leading scorer in the history of the Cameroon national team.

bio|03-10|1985|Κονσταντίν Τσερνιένκο|Konstantin Chernenko|Konstantin Chernenko was a Soviet politician. He became general secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1984, already elderly and ill. He died after 13 months, and he was succeeded by Mikhail Gorbachev.

bio|03-11|222|Ηλιογάβαλος|Elagabalus|Elagabalus was a Roman emperor from 218 to 222. He was born in Syria and was a priest of the sun god. His reign became famous for its unusual religious innovations. He was murdered by the Praetorians.

bio|03-11|1544|Τορκουάτο Τάσσο|Torquato Tasso|Torquato Tasso was an Italian poet of the Renaissance. He wrote the epic poem "Jerusalem Delivered", about the First Crusade, and the pastoral drama "Aminta". He suffered from mental problems.

bio|03-11|1916|Χάρολντ Ουίλσον|Harold Wilson|Harold Wilson was a British Labour politician. He was prime minister twice, from 1964 to 1970 and from 1974 to 1976. He was known for his reforms in education.

bio|03-11|1931|Ρούπερτ Μέρντοχ|Rupert Murdoch|Rupert Murdoch was born in Australia. He is the founder of News Corporation and the owner of many newspapers and television networks, such as Fox News and The Times of London. He is one of the most powerful people in the media.

bio|03-11|1952|Ντάγκλας Άνταμς|Douglas Adams|Douglas Adams was an English science fiction writer. He wrote "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy", a comic series that began as a radio programme. He died in 2001.

bio|03-11|1955|Αλεξάντερ Φλέμινγκ|Alexander Fleming|Alexander Fleming was a Scottish bacteriologist. In 1928 he discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic. In 1945 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Florey and Chain.

bio|03-11|1978|Ντιντιέ Ντρογκμπά|Didier Drogba|Didier Drogba is a former Ivorian footballer. He played for Chelsea and Marseille, and scored the goal that brought Chelsea the Champions League in 2012. He is also a humanitarian.

bio|03-11|2002|Τζέιμς Τόμπιν|James Tobin|James Tobin was an American economist. He studied finance and proposed a tax on international currency transactions, the "Tobin tax". In 1981 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.

bio|03-11|2006|Σλόμπονταν Μιλόσεβιτς|Slobodan Milosevic|Slobodan Milosevic was a Serbian politician. He was president of Serbia and of Yugoslavia and is responsible for wars in the Balkans. He was tried by the International Criminal Tribunal in The Hague and died in prison in 2006, before the verdict.

bio|03-12|1685|Τζωρτζ Μπέρκλεϋ|George Berkeley|George Berkeley was an Irish philosopher and bishop. He argued for subjective idealism, with the phrase "to be is to be perceived". He wrote "A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge".

bio|03-12|1824|Γκούσταβ Κίρχοφ|Gustav Kirchhoff|Gustav Kirchhoff was a German physicist. He formulated Kirchhoff's rules for electrical circuits and developed spectroscopy with Bunsen. Together they discovered the elements caesium and rubidium.

bio|03-12|1863|Γκαμπριέλε Ντ' Ανούντσιο|Gabriele D'Annunzio|Gabriele D'Annunzio was an Italian poet, writer and soldier. His work has a particularly elegant style. In the 1920s he became a symbol of Italian nationalism and influenced fascism.

bio|03-12|1922|Τζακ Κέρουακ|Jack Kerouac|Jack Kerouac was an American writer and one of the central figures of the Beat Generation. He wrote the novel "On the Road" in 1957, an account of journeys that became a symbol of a generation.

bio|03-12|1925|Σουν Γιατ-Σεν|Sun Yat-sen|Sun Yat-sen was a Chinese revolutionary and politician. He led the revolution of 1911 that overthrew the Qing dynasty and became the first president of the Republic of China. He is regarded as the "father of the nation" in China and in Taiwan.

bio|03-12|1942|Ουίλιαμ Χένρι Μπραγκ|William Henry Bragg|William Henry Bragg was an English physicist. Together with his son Lawrence he developed X-ray crystallography, and in 1915 they shared the Nobel Prize in Physics. He was the first to be honoured together with his son.

bio|03-12|1946|Λάιζα Μινέλι|Liza Minnelli|Liza Minnelli is an American actress and singer, the daughter of Judy Garland. She won the Oscar for Best Actress for "Cabaret" in 1972 and has been honoured with Emmy and Tony awards.

bio|03-12|1947|Μιτ Ρόμνεϊ|Mitt Romney|Mitt Romney is an American politician and businessman. He was governor of Massachusetts and the Republican candidate for the presidency in 2012, when he lost to Barack Obama. From 2019 to 2025 he was a senator for Utah.

bio|03-12|2015|Τέρι Πράτσετ|Terry Pratchett|Terry Pratchett was an English writer of fantasy and satire. He created the "Discworld" series, with dozens of novels. He died in 2015 of Alzheimer's disease.

bio|03-13|1711|Νικολά Μπουαλώ|Nicolas Boileau|Nicolas Boileau was a French poet and critic. In his work "The Art of Poetry" he set out the rules of French classicism. He also wrote satires and was an important figure in the age of Louis XIV.

bio|03-13|1741|Ιωσήφ Β΄ των Αψβούργων|Joseph II|Joseph II was emperor of the Holy Roman Empire from 1765 and ruler of the Habsburg lands. He was a representative of enlightened despotism. He abolished serfdom and imposed religious tolerance.

bio|03-13|1781|Καρλ Φρίντριχ Σίνκελ|Karl Friedrich Schinkel|Karl Friedrich Schinkel was a German architect and painter. He designed many neoclassical buildings in Berlin, such as the Altes Museum and the Schauspielhaus. He also drew proposals for a palace on the Acropolis of Athens.

bio|03-13|1855|Πέρσιβαλ Λόουελ|Percival Lowell|Percival Lowell was an American astronomer. He founded the Lowell Observatory in Arizona and argued that there were canals on Mars. His search for a "Planet X" later led to the discovery of Pluto.

bio|03-13|1881|Αλέξανδρος Β'|Alexander II|Alexander II was tsar of Russia from 1855 to 1881. He carried out reforms, mainly the abolition of serfdom in 1861, and is called "the Liberator". He was murdered in 1881 by revolutionaries in Saint Petersburg.

bio|03-13|1901|Μπέντζαμιν Χάρρισον|Benjamin Harrison|Benjamin Harrison was the 23rd president of the United States, from 1889 to 1893. He was the grandson of President William Henry Harrison. During his presidency the anti-monopoly laws were passed.

bio|03-13|1907|Μίρτσεα Ελιάντε|Mircea Eliade|Mircea Eliade was a Romanian historian of religions and writer. He lived in the United States and wrote "The Sacred and the Profane" and "A History of Religious Ideas". He also wrote literature.

bio|03-13|1975|Ίβο Άντριτς|Ivo Andric|Ivo Andric was a Yugoslav writer and diplomat. He wrote the novel "The Bridge on the Drina", which tells the history of Bosnia. In 1961 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|03-14|1820|Βίκτωρ Εμμανουήλ Β΄|Victor Emmanuel II|Victor Emmanuel II was king of Sardinia and in 1861 became the first king of a united Italy. Cavour and Garibaldi helped in the unification.

bio|03-14|1854|Πάουλ Έρλιχ|Paul Ehrlich|Paul Ehrlich was a German doctor and scientist. He is regarded as a pioneer of chemotherapy and developed salvarsan against syphilis. In 1908 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

bio|03-14|1879|Άλμπερτ Αϊνστάιν|Albert Einstein|Albert Einstein was born in Germany and was a physicist. He developed the special and the general theory of relativity and explained the photoelectric effect, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921. He lived in the United States from 1933.

bio|03-14|1883|Καρλ Μαρξ|Karl Marx|Karl Marx was born in Trier and was a philosopher, economist and revolutionary. He wrote the "Communist Manifesto" with Friedrich Engels and "Capital" on his own. He died in London in 1883.

bio|03-14|1933|Μάικλ Κέιν|Michael Caine|Michael Caine is an English actor. He became known for films such as "Alfie", "The Italian Job" and "The Dark Knight". He won two Oscars for Best Supporting Actor, for "Hannah and Her Sisters" and "The Cider House Rules".

bio|03-14|1958|Αλβέρτος Β΄|Albert II|Albert II has been sovereign prince of Monaco since 2005, when his father Rainier III died. He is the son of the actress Grace Kelly. He has competed in the Olympic Games as a bobsledder.
